Samantha — thanks again for working through the order form redlines on the call this morning. Attaching our v2 redline (redline_orderform_v2.pdf) with two high-priority asks we need to resolve before legal signs: 

1) Invoicing entity and PO flow
   - Brightline to confirm the legal entity that will receive invoices. We propose invoicing Brightline Ltd (EU entity) for EU region usage; if US entity preferred, please confirm.
2) Tax / VAT handling for EU customers
   - For EU shipments, we propose contract language that allocates VAT/responsibility to Brightline and adds a reverse-charge placeholder where applicable. If Brightline requires Redwood to gross up or collect VAT, flag now.

Other items (quick):
- Minimum commit reconciliation: Redwood will invoice quarterly against the commit; any shortfall will be invoiced on next quarter invoice.
- Net terms: Redwood standard is Net30; Finance is open to Net45 for this deal (see Marcus Cc'd).
- Attachments: redline_orderform_v2.pdf (our suggested changes).

Requested next steps:
- Samantha: please confirm invoicing entity + VAT expectation by end of day Wednesday so legal can finalize language.
- If Brightline needs Net45, confirm explicitly so Marcus can sign off.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Kim — thanks for the summary and the redline. Quick answers below and a couple of asks from our side: 

- Invoicing entity: Please invoice Brightline International Ltd (EU VAT ID: GB999999999). We will provide a PO after signature.
- VAT: We expect to be responsible for VAT via reverse-charge where permitted. We cannot accept Redwood grossing up VAT charges. Please include reverse-charge language; we'll push back if Redwood remains liable.
- Net terms: Net45 is acceptable. Finance will process on Net45 once PoS signed.
- Invoicing cadence: Can Redwood split invoicing into quarterly invoices aligned to calendar quarters? Brightline prefers not to receive monthly invoices for forecasting reasons.

Attached are our in-line comments (Brightline-comments.docx). We also flagged an ask to add a short clause about withholding taxes for cross-border services — we need Redwood to confirm Redwood will not withhold by default and any withholding will be agreed and evidenced.

If you can incorporate these items, we can sign within 3 business days.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Sr. Procurement Manager
Brightline

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Mar 2028 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Final redline capture & tax allocation roadmap

Kim / Marcus — forwarding Brightline's comments and my proposed legal language below. High level: we can accept Brightline's asks with tightened wording on withholding and a small change to the invoice cadence to protect Redwood's revenue recognition and minimum commit reconciliation. 

Suggested contract snippets (to add to order form / appendix):

1) VAT / Tax Clause (proposed):
"The parties agree that, where applicable, the reverse charge mechanism shall apply and Brightline shall be responsible for any VAT, GST or similar transaction taxes arising from the provision of Services in the EU. Redwood will render invoices exclusive of VAT when Brightline provides valid VAT registration details. Any taxes required to be withheld by Brightline under local law must be evidenced and mutually agreed in writing prior to withholding."

2) Invoicing cadence & Minimum Commit reconciliation:
"Invoices will be issued on a quarterly basis (calendar quarters) for consumption and commit reconciliation. Redwood will issue an invoice for any shortfall to the aggregate minimum commit within 30 days of the close of the quarter. Parties agree that quarterly invoices may include aggregated line items to reflect commit reconciliation; detailed consumption reports will be provided as an appendix. Failure to reconcile within 90 days will not relieve Brightline of payment obligations."

3) Net terms: Net45 accepted per Marcus' sign-off.

Action items: 
- Marcus: confirm Net45 OK for revenue recognition / cashflow (short note).
- Kim: if you want tighter language around capping withholding or adding an indemnity, say so — otherwise I will include above on next draft.

Ben
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
